doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: Rock and roll musicians met in San Francisco
summary: Percy defends his own way of playing and recalls meeting rock players in San Francisco with large equipment.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: But I will still say so. I will still, this is my motto. I like the music. The way you play it the way you want to play it. But I love it, understand? Because I don't know the other way to do what I'm doing. Well, you come up with that. And I can't change it. I can't change it. But I don't say that rock and roll is good for people who like it. But I don't say that's... Them boys don't... And all them boys come from school. School band. Them boys can read. Don't you worry what they can't do. They think... We've got plenty of good rock and roll musicians. I met a gang of them. You understand? Something in two... No, that's what we met, you know... San Francisco. Graceful Deed. What?

Had that million dollar... Not a million dollar head. About $30,000 equipment. What? Graceful Deed. What? Who are them people stuck? Graceful Deed. San Francisco. Yeah. We talk with them people there. They said the amplifiers was right. Them boys. Fillmore West. And there was...

They went to a lot playing. This was down low. And you could, every man was doing this, you could enjoy it. Man can't do drummers. One of the things. Yeah. Two drummers. When we got there, I said look here. Boy.
